items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: But it's Bunny Berrigan they're playing really.

ctx.x: Would there be much of what you might call improvised solo playing in those days? Or was it mostly a matter of taking a break or a few bars or something in...?

Yes, there was much improvising. Not all the time, no. Guys would take something somebody else had played, they'd heard play, you know, and put it in there. It's like they used to play a very good solo on... They thought it was a really great thing to do, you know. They did "Singin' The Blues." It was a masterpiece thing, like everyone wants to play it... Today they try to play it... [SINGS A REFRAIN] And ...(?)... has been recorded(?). But invariably they want to play his solo. Everybody...you know... But it's…
That's the way it was in those days, too, because you'd hear somebody play something, and...you know, copy it. It would help them learn(?) (?) a great deal.
